title: Hāna Health Center land change for housing
summary: The Hāna Advisory Committee recommended approving a change of Hāna Health Center land from agriculture to rural district to allow six workforce housing units and a specialty clinic, with priority for Hāna residents where practical. The project must go back to the state land board for final approval after the district change.

timeline.text: The motion passed with five votes in favor.
The motion said that, where practical and while meeting staffing needs, Hāna residents get priority for the housing.
A member moved to recommend approval with the department's two conditions plus housing priority for Hāna residents where practical.
The applicant's consultant said the project must go back to the state land board for final approval after the district change.
The applicant said employees could stay in the housing as long as they are employed, with no set time limit.
The applicant said rent cannot be charged on the state-leased land, so housing would be part of employee pay.
The two studios are for visiting specialists who stay two or three days.
A member asked whether the housing could give priority to Hāna residents.
Hāna Health wants to build six workforce housing units for its employees.
The change would allow six workforce housing units and a specialty clinic.
One resident testified in support of the change.
The only item was a public hearing on a Council resolution to change Hāna Health Center land from the state agriculture district to the rural district.
The chair said he has no financial or other interest in Hāna Health beyond being a client, and would not step aside.
